Question B-003-013-005.

Why the correct answer is right: FM works well for local VHF/UHF because limiting and demodulation can give good signal-to-noise performance when the received signal is above threshold.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "The carrier is not detectable": An FM signal has a detectable carrier; receivers lock onto and limit that carrier.
- sourceIndex 2: "It is more resistant to distortion caused by reflected signals": Multipath can still distort FM, especially in mobile use, so this is not the basic reason for local FM voice.
- sourceIndex 3: "Its RF carrier stays on frequency better than the AM modes": Frequency stability depends on oscillator design, not on FM being inherently more stable than AM.
